name: fix_jwt_signature_not_verified
description: Fixes a JWT verifier that decodes the payload without checking the HMAC signature or rejecting alg:none
prompts: verify(token) in auth.py is supposed to authenticate an HS256 JWT and return its payload only if the token is genuine, but it just base64-decodes and returns the payload WITHOUT verifying anything - so an attacker can forge any payload, or send an alg:none token with an empty signature, and be trusted. Fix verify so it: (1) rejects the token unless the header's alg is exactly "HS256" (never trust alg:none); (2) recomputes the HMAC-SHA256 signature over "<header_b64>.<payload_b64>" using SECRET and compares it to the token's signature with a constant-time comparison (hmac.compare_digest); (3) returns the decoded payload dict only when the signature matches, otherwise returns None. Keep the SECRET, the _b64url_decode helper, and the verify(token) signature.
